newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Latest Czech data show budget deficit in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Latest Czech data show budget deficit in 1996.

text.p: The Czech 1996 state budget was in deficit by 1.7 billion crowns as of January 14, one day before the deadline for entities to bill the state for services provdided during the year, a finance ministry official said on Wednesday.
"(We expect) the definitive results for 1996 will range around a deficit of 1.7 billion crowns," said Miroslav Havel, deputy finance minister, in testimony to the parliamentary budget committtee.
He said that as of January 14, revenues for the state totalled 482.8 billion crowns, while expenditures were 484.5 billion crowns.
Havel added that some additional bills may be delivered in the days following the deadline, which could inflate expenditures further.

Parliamentary budget committee chairman Jozef Wagner said at the session that though he was not upset with the slight deficit in 1996, he was concerned with the effects any changes in payments may have on the 1997 budget.
The deficit does not come as a shock to many since the government said in December that it was trying to hold an expected deficit to around one billion crowns.

But last week, the government delayed payments and forced some early collections, including a 650 million crown early repayment on credit to the Deposit Insurance Fund, in an attempt to claim its fourth straight budget surplus in 1996.
